blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines—It’s easy to assume that Rey Remogat’s performance against defending champion La Salle on Sunday was to avenge University of the Philippines’ loss in last year’s UAAP Finals. Remogat, however, made one thing clear: he’s moved on from last season’s heartbreak, and he’s focused on the present. “I don’t have any more frustrations from last year, but in our last two losses, I wanted to achieve something as a person and we wanted to achieve something as a team,” he said after the Fighting Maroons’ 80-76 victory. “We just wanted to get this win and we just want to get […]...
